applies_why: The judge text makes the absence of an explicit naming of whose body is the channel the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the thing K-S2 governs.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'does not state a link or its contrary' — I weighed whether the judge used lack of explicit statement as the forbidden ground for UNDERDETERMINED, or instead treated the verse as itself open under the definition; the deciding phrase is 'without naming whose body is the channel,' which is a lack-of-explicit-statement reason.
why: Because the judge's stated reason is that the text does not name whose body is the channel, it makes a verse's failure to state the link the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2.
